title: Subscriber-facing regression containment and expedited patch coordination across hosted/dedicated/private
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: A customer-reported degradation surfaced during a mixed-environment model rollout. Symptoms include increased hallucinations and higher latency for a subset of subscribers on Dedicated hosts while Hosted traffic exhibited degraded quality in canary slices. This ticket coordinates containment, fast patch engineering, and cross-team customer comms for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope: - Identify immediate containment (traffic routing, tenant pinning, synthetic traffic to validate fixes). - Produce an urgent, minimal-impact patch (code or config) and test it across environments. - Coordinate KV cache reconciliation and model variant pinning to avoid stale context causing regressions. - Provide clear customer-facing status updates and post-incident remediation plan.

Why now: Escalation from an enterprise customer resulted in an SLA-impacting support case and on-call involvement. We must both stabilize surface-level regressions and create a repeatable runbook for similar cross-environment rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Affected subscribers routed away from regressed variant without >5% request-rate drop in unaffected routes.
Urgent patch merged and canary-tested in Hosted and Dedicated within the cycle window.
KV cache reconciliation steps executed and documented; no stale-context errors in 48h post-fix in sampled tenants.
Customer notified with root-cause hypothesis and ETA for full remediation; follow-up postmortem scheduled.
Playbook for cross-environment urgent rollback/pin now in Console runbooks and linked to incident postmortem.
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: Collect correlation IDs and affected tenant IDs from support ticket and live logs (Edge & Ingest traces).
2) Contain: Use routing policy to pin affected tenants to last-known-good model variant in Dedicated and Private; create a Hosted override flag for canary slices.
3) Validate: Run targeted synthetic prompt set from Canary harness and compare generation quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/CR-qa heuristics) against baseline dashboard.
4) Patch: Branch minimal behavioral fix (model config or tokenizer edge-case normalization) and open hotpatch PR; include model-variant compatibility tests.
5) Deploy: Canary in Hosted (1% traffic) and Dedicated slice (single pod) with KV cache warmup; monitor rollback thresholds (latency, error-rate, quality regressions).
6) Reconcile: Rehydrate/flush KV cache for pinned tenants where applicable, validate sequence alignment and token-offset mappings after patch.
7) Communicate: Post interim update to customer-facing status page, Slack #enterprise-escalations, and on-call channel; coordinate support messaging and rate-limit exemptions if needed.
8) Postmortem: After stabilization, run full RCA, list prevention actions, and attach runbook updates to this ticket.
